prior_importants.description: Once `pup-gate` is required, an open PR that an older pup gated (head still at the pin, no status) cannot be merged. `planRegate` refuses to re-gate it with "nothing new to gate… Merge it on GitHub", which GitHub now blocks. The new docs forbid setting the status by hand, so nothing can unblock it.

On a branch that is protected but has no required status checks, GitHub probably answers `PATCH .../protection/required_status_checks` with 404 "Required status checks not enabled". That would leave no working command for this state except the `PUT`, which the ADR itself says wipes existing protection.

findings.description: LOOP.md leaves out the ADR's caveat for the Settings > Branches step: the page lists only checks the repo has seen recently, so run one `pup merge --pr` first if `pup-gate` is missing. An operator who follows only LOOP.md on a repo that has never run `pup merge --pr` since decision 182 finds no `pup-gate` to add, and nothing tells them why. Add that clause, or point to the ADR for this step.

LOOP.md has the conductor hand the operator 'the sha the refusal names' from the conductor's own re-gate. ADR 0182 instead has the operator run `pup merge <task> --pr` and read the sha from that refusal themselves. Following the ADR here would stop a steered conductor from passing on an unmeasured head, such as one named in a fresh-base or pinRegatedHead refusal.
